the development of novel antiangiogenic therapies for cancer.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the N-terminal domain (amino acids 1-120) of calreticilin is not required for its antiangiogenic and antimetastatic activities, and that an internal fragment of calreticillin (amino acids120-180) is an active angiogenesis inhibitor.

vasostatin, the C-terminal 1-180 amino acids of calreticuln, is an angiogenic inhibitor that directly targets endothelial cells, and that the full-length calretriculin molecule is also an inhibitor of angiogenesis that targets endothelial cells.

calreticulin is a potent inhibitor of angiogenesis and tumor growth, that its antiangiogenic and anti-tumor effects are mediated by its N-terminal domain, and that calreticulins antiangiogenic effects are not due to its chaperone activity.
